title: Automated Logistics Documentation Synthesis
business: Global logistics firms managing thousands of daily shipping manifests and compliance documents.
problem: Manual extraction of compliance data from massive, unstructured shipment manifests leads to high latency and frequent human error in customs declarations.
solution: Utilizing GPT-4.1's 1M token context window to ingest entire multi-page manifests and using function calling to map extracted data directly into structured customs schemas.
steps: Upload multi-page PDF manifests as file objects to the Assistants API.
Define a structured JSON schema for customs compliance fields.
Invoke GPT-4.1 via the Chat Completions endpoint with function calling enabled to map manifest text to the schema.
Validate the structured output against the internal database before final submission.
outcome: Significant reduction in document processing time and improved consistency in customs data entry without the overhead of reasoning-heavy models.
limitation: Because GPT-4.1 is a non-reasoning model, it may struggle with highly ambiguous or contradictory document clauses; verify accuracy by cross-referencing extracted fields against historical compliance logs.
